les: Afrika, sy oseane en sy lande
kaps_punt: Ligging van Afrika op 'n wêreldkaart en aardbol (oorsig van Graad 4); Oseane rondom Afrika (name en liggings); Konsepte van lande en grense; Lande van Afrika: Ligging van alle lande*

items.bewering: Afrika is die tweede grootste kontinent op aarde, en net Asië is groter.
items.bron: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Africa' (britannica.com/place/Africa): 'the second largest continent (after Asia), covering about one-fifth of the total land surface of Earth'.

items.bewering: Op 'n wêreldkaart of 'n aardbol sien jy dat die ewenaar deur Afrika loop. 'n Deel van die kontinent lê dus noord van die ewenaar en 'n ander deel suid daarvan.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Africa' (the continent is cut almost equally in two by the Equator in its north-south extent, roughly 37°N to 35°S); WorldAtlas, 'Which Hemisphere Has The Largest Area Covered By Land?'.

items.bewering: Die deel in die noorde is baie breër as die deel in die suide.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Africa': the bulge of western Africa lies north of the Equator. Africa's east-west extreme points, Pointe des Almadies/Cap Vert in Senegal (about 14.7°N) and Ras Hafun in Somalia (about 10.4°N), are both north of the Equator and about 7 400 km apart. South of the Equator the continent narrows towards the Cape (Geography of Africa / Extreme points of Africa reference pages).

items.bewering: Daarom lê die grootste deel van Afrika se grond noord van die ewenaar.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Africa': because of the western bulge, 'the greater part of Africa's territory lies north of the Equator'. WorldAtlas gives about 66% north of the Equator. The 'daarom' reasoning holds because the equator divides the continent's north-south extent roughly in half.

items.bewering: Die Atlantiese Oseaan lê wes van Afrika en die Indiese Oseaan oos daarvan.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Africa' (bordered by the Atlantic to the west and the Indian Ocean to the east).

items.bewering: Hulle ontmoet mekaar aan die suidpunt van Afrika.
items.bron: International Hydrographic Organization limits (1953 Special Publication 23, citing the earlier IHB report): the boundary between the Atlantic and Indian Oceans is the meridian of 20°E through Cape Agulhas (34°50'S 20°00'E), which is Africa's southernmost point. Reported via the International Hydrographic Review (journals.lib.unb.ca) and southafrica.info. The lesson says 'suidpunt' and not Cape Point, so it avoids the common Cape Point error.

items.bewering: Die Middellandse See lê noord van Afrika en die Rooi See in die noordooste.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Mediterranean Sea' (separates Europe from Africa, so it lies to Africa's north). Britannica, 'Red Sea' summary and Britannica Kids: a narrow inland sea between north-eastern Africa and the Arabian Peninsula.

items.bewering: Hierdie twee is kleiner seë en nie oseane nie.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Mediterranean Sea': an intercontinental sea joined to the Atlantic through the Strait of Gibraltar. Britannica Kids, 'Red Sea': an inland sea connected to the Indian Ocean through the Gulf of Aden. Both are seas joined to the oceans, and neither appears among the five major oceans (Britannica Kids, 'ocean').

items.bewering: Party mense praat van Afrika asof dit een land is. Afrika is egter 'n kontinent en nie 'n land nie.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Africa' (a continent of many countries). The misconception that Africa is one country is widely documented, for example on Africa.com ('10 common misconceptions and stereotypes about Africa'). That page is a commentary source, not a reference work, but the claim only says that some people speak this way.

items.bewering: 'n Land is 'n gebied met sy eie grense wat homself regeer. Dit het sy eie regering en is nie deel van 'n ander land nie.
items.bron: Montevideo Convention (1933), Article 1: a state has a defined territory, a permanent population, a government and the capacity to enter into relations with other states, and independence is generally read into the government criterion. The lesson's wording is an accurate simplification of an independent state, and it is the sense the '54 lande' count uses. Note: in ordinary English 'country' is sometimes also used for parts of a state, such as Scotland. That is not an error here, because the lesson defines its own term consistently.

items.bewering: Afrika het 54 lande wat deur die Verenigde Nasies erken word.
items.bron: Africa has 54 UN member states. South Sudan was admitted on 14 July 2011 as the 193rd UN member and the 54th from Africa (Guinness World Records, 'Newest independent country'; WorldAtlas, 'Which Country Is The Latest To Join The UN'). Western Sahara (SADR) is an African Union member but not a UN member, which is why the AU counts 55. The lesson's 'deur die VN erken' correctly scopes the figure.

items.bewering: 'n Grens is die lyn wat een gebied van 'n ander gebied skei. Tussen twee lande wys dit waar die een land eindig en die ander begin.
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'border': 'the line that divides two countries or areas'. National Geographic Education, encyclopedic entry 'border'.

items.bewering: Party grense volg 'n rivier, en ander is reguit lyne wat op 'n kaart getrek is.
items.bron: Peer-reviewed study 'Endogenous Colonial Borders: Precolonial States and Geography in the Partition of Africa', American Political Science Review (Cambridge University Press, 2024): about 63% of Africa's bilateral borders follow water bodies (rivers, lakes, watersheds) as a primary feature, and about 37% include straight latitude or longitude lines, mostly in deserts.

items.bewering: Mense besluit waar elke grens loop, ook waar dit 'n rivier volg.
items.bron: Same APSR study (colonial negotiators chose which rivers, watersheds and lines to use). A concrete example of a human choice about a river border: the Cape Colony and German South West Africa border was set at the high-water mark on the northern bank of the Orange River, not mid-stream, and Namibia's constitution places it mid-river, which is still unresolved (Travel News Namibia; widely reported).

items.bewering: 'n Politieke kaart wys die lande van Afrika, hulle grense en die name van plekke.
items.bron: WorldAtlas, 'Political and physical maps' (worldatlas.com/geography/political-and-physical-maps.html): political maps show country boundaries, cities and administrative regions, as opposed to the terrain shown on physical maps.

items.bewering: Jy hoef nie al 54 lande uit jou kop te leer nie. Jy kan eerder op die kaart aflees waar elke land lê.
items.bron: The count of 54 matches the UN-member count confirmed above. The rest is a study instruction, not a factual claim.

items.bewering: Net noord van Suid-Afrika lê Botswana, tussen Namibië in die weste en Zimbabwe in die ooste.
items.bron: CIA World Factbook, 'Botswana': location 'Southern Africa, north of South Africa'. Britannica, 'Botswana': bounded by Namibia to the west and north, Zambia and Zimbabwe to the northeast, and South Africa to the southeast and south. Zimbabwe lies to the north-east rather than due east, which is acceptable at this level. The lesson does not claim the list of neighbours is complete, so leaving out the roughly 150 m Zambia contact at Kazungula is not an error.

items.bewering: 'n Wêreldkaart wat Afrika wys, met die ewenaar wat deur die kontinent loop. Die Atlantiese Oseaan lê wes van Afrika en die Indiese Oseaan oos daarvan, en die kaart wys waar die twee aan die suidpunt van Afrika bymekaarkom. Die Middellandse See lê noord van Afrika en die Rooi See in die noordooste.
items.blok: kaart: Oseane en seë rondom Afrika
items.bron: Same claims as the study block 'Oseane en seë rondom Afrika' and 'Afrika op die aardbol'. Sources as above (Britannica; IHO 20°E meridian at Cape Agulhas).

items.bewering: Die name van Suid-Afrika, Botswana, Namibië en Zimbabwe moet leesbaar wees, want die studieteks lees Botswana se ligging tussen hulle af.
items.bron: Botswana's neighbours are as in Britannica, 'Botswana', and the CIA World Factbook (see above).

items.bewering: oseaan: Een van die baie groot waterruimtes om die kontinente.
items.bron: Britannica Kids, 'ocean': the large bodies of salt water into which the world ocean is divided, which surround the continents. The five major oceans are the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic.

items.bewering: land: 'n Gebied met sy eie grense wat homself regeer, soos Suid-Afrika.
items.bron: Montevideo Convention Article 1 criteria (see the study-block item). South Africa is a sovereign UN member state.

items.bewering: regering: Die groep mense wat 'n land lei en besluite daarvoor neem.
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary / Learner's Dictionary, 'government': 'the group of people who control and make decisions for a country, state, etc.'

items.bewering: grens: Die lyn wat een gebied van 'n ander gebied skei.
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'border': 'the line that divides two countries or areas'.

items.bewering: politieke kaart: 'n Kaart wat lande, hulle grense en die name van plekke wys.
items.bron: WorldAtlas, 'Political and physical maps': political maps show country boundaries, cities and administrative regions.

items.bewering: Verenigde Nasies: 'n Groep waarin byna al die lande van die wêreld saamwerk.
items.bron: The UN has 193 member states. The Holy See and Palestine are non-member observer states, and a few entities such as Taiwan and Kosovo are not members (Congressional Research Service report R43614, 'Membership in the United Nations and Its Specialized Agencies'; WorldAtlas, 'Which countries are not members of the United Nations'). 'Byna al' is accurate.

opsomming: All 25 checkable claims are confirmed, including both superlatives ('tweede grootste kontinent' and 'grootste deel ... noord van die ewenaar'), the Atlantic-Indian meeting at Africa's southern tip (IHO 20°E meridian at Cape Agulhas), the 54 UN-recognised countries, and Botswana's position between Namibia and Zimbabwe; the lesson contains no analogies, and nothing needs fixing.
